tasks.name_en: Take one bowl from a kitchen work surface
tasks.name_ja: キッチンの作業面からボウルを一つ取る
instruction_variants: Take the bowl from the kitchen work surface.
Pick up the bowl and hold it securely.
キッチンの作業面からボウルを取り、安定して持ってください。
tasks.notes: Source example: the EPIC-KITCHENS VISOR supplementary material uses the illustrative sequence ‘take bowl’ then ‘wash bowl’ to explain continuity between adjacent action clips. It does not provide an annotation row ID or exact starting surface; a stable reachable work surface and held-bowl endpoint are explicit Task Atlas collection-design assumptions that operationalize the verb label. Proposed cross-resource mapping: the EPIC noun class ‘bowl’ is associated here with the existing reusable YCB instance ycb_024_bowl. This is a proposal for a candidate object, not an assertion that the recorded bowl is the YCB model or that the model is visually, physically, or simulator compatible. Atlas graph walk: this TaskInstance --acts_on--> ycb_024_bowl --instance_of--> concept:object_dish (two existing Atlas relation edges). This is the first of two distinct sibling primitives under object_dish; its documented companion is task_reference_epic_kitchens_wash_bowl_round1.

tasks.name_en: Wash one bowl at a kitchen wash station
tasks.name_ja: キッチンの洗い場でボウルを一つ洗う
instruction_variants: Wash the bowl at the kitchen sink and leave it on the wash-station surface.
Clean the bowl with the wash tool, then check that visible soil is gone.
ボウルを洗い場で洗い、目に見える汚れが落ちたことを確認してください。
tasks.notes: Source example: the EPIC-KITCHENS VISOR supplementary material explicitly gives ‘take bowl’ followed by ‘wash bowl’ as an example of object continuity across adjacent clips. It does not specify dirt state, exact wash procedure, sink setup, cleaning tool, or endpoint; those are bounded collection-design assumptions in this proposal. The YCB sponge is an Atlas helper-object choice and is not a tool identity reported by that example. Proposed cross-resource mapping: the EPIC noun class ‘bowl’ is associated with existing reusable YCB instance ycb_024_bowl, without claiming that the recorded object is the YCB model or that it is compatible with a water-based wash setup, robot, or simulator. Atlas graph walk: this TaskInstance --acts_on--> ycb_024_bowl --instance_of--> concept:object_dish (two existing Atlas relation edges). This is a distinct sibling primitive to task_reference_epic_kitchens_take_bowl_round1 under the same existing ObjectClass.

procedures.label: Pick up and hold one bowl

steps.description: Locate the bowl on the declared stable source surface.
Establish a stable grasp on the bowl.
Lift the bowl clear of the surface.
Verify the bowl is held and no longer supported by the source surface.

success_criteria: The bowl is lifted clear of the source surface and remains securely held without visible damage.
setup: Use a level, stable kitchen work surface with clear access around the candidate bowl.
Record that the candidate YCB bowl is a proposed cross-resource mapping, then confirm its physical geometry and grasp suitability separately before any collection trial.
reset: Return the bowl to its marked source position and verify that it is stable and undamaged.
quality_checks: Confirm the bowl cleared the surface, remained controlled, and was not chipped or dropped.
failure_modes: Collision with adjacent objects or bowl damage

requirements.reason: Use the existing kitchen scene type for a separately staged bowl-washing episode.
Candidate reusable object mapped from the EPIC bowl label; matching the recorded bowl and model has not been established.
Proposed reusable helper object for a controlled wash trial; it is not identified by the cited example.
External sink and safe-water resource; no particular fixture is specified by the cited action example.
External stable surface where the bowl can be supported during setup and post-wash inspection.
Proposed observable setup to define a measurable wash goal; the source does not describe soil or water state.
Collection-design requirement for holding and manipulating the bowl; no platform execution evidence is claimed.
Collection-design requirement for the proposed bowl/tool contact phase.

procedures.label: Wash one bowl and verify visible soil removal

steps.description: Locate the bowl, wash tool, and declared wash station.
Hold or stabilize the bowl safely over the wash station.
Apply the wash tool to the bowl surfaces under the declared water conditions.
Check the bowl for visible remaining soil and record the result.

success_criteria: Visible soil is removed from the bowl, and the bowl remains intact on the stable wash-station surface.
setup: Provide a stable basin-side staging surface, safe water supply, and the YCB sponge as a proposed helper; do not assume compatibility with the source video object.
Use only a controlled, documented, non-hazardous removable soil surrogate; protect nearby electrical equipment and the work area from water.
Verify that the selected bowl, sponge, and wash setup tolerate water contact before the trial.
reset: Return the bowl and sponge to their recorded staging positions, drain and dry the station, and remove the soil surrogate.
quality_checks: Record visible soil before and after, water containment, bowl stability, and any damage.
failure_modes: Remaining soil after the wash episode
Bowl dropped, chipped, or left unstable
Water escapes the controlled wash area
Candidate bowl or tool proves unsuitable for water contact

evidence.scope: The official VISOR supplementary material describes adjacent action clips using the example ‘take bowl’ followed by ‘wash bowl’. This supports two candidate bowl-focused interaction labels and their proposed adjacency.
evidence.limitations: This is an illustrative example in the dataset-method supplementary material, not an identified annotation-row ID. It does not specify exact initial or goal states, a robotic procedure, a YCB object identity, asset compatibility, robot execution, or population frequency. EPIC-KITCHENS is a selected egocentric video dataset; action examples or counts must not be interpreted as household prevalence.
evidence.notes: Primary source supplementary material hosted by OpenReview for the VISOR paper. It explicitly mentions the take-bowl then wash-bowl continuity example. No annotation ID is inferred or invented.

evidence.scope: The official release describes ground-truth action segments with action/verb/noun labels and start/end times; it gives ‘take plate’ as a train annotation-format example. The official noun-class table includes the noun key bowl in the crockery category.
evidence.limitations: The README format example is ‘take plate’, not a bowl annotation row. It establishes how source action labels are represented but does not identify an instance of the YCB bowl, define robot feasibility, or estimate household task frequency.
evidence.notes: Primary release documentation. draft_notes: EPIC-KITCHENS round 1 contains two distinct proposed primitive tasks: take bowl, then wash bowl. Their shared local Atlas path is TaskInstance --acts_on--> ycb_024_bowl --instance_of--> concept:object_dish, so they are sibling task instances at the same ObjectClass after ascending two hierarchy edges. The source supplementary material explicitly uses these labels in an adjacent-action continuity example, but does not expose a specific annotation-row ID in that example. The official release README provides the action/verb/noun annotation format and a separate ‘take plate’ format example; no row-level annotation or count was retrieved here. Mapping the source noun bowl to YCB ycb_024_bowl is proposed only; the YCB bowl and helper sponge are candidate reusable assets, not source object matches. Task suitability remains proposed; population frequency, robot execution, asset compatibility, and all durations remain unknown/null. Do not interpret EPIC dataset activity counts or examples as household prevalence.
